question: Which crop is referred to as the 'golden fibre' in India? (RPF Constable 2024 (11/03/2025) Shift 1)
options: Silk
Jute
Wheat
Cotton
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Jute

Explanation:
Jute is called 'Golden Fibre' in India because of its golden color and high economic value. It is a natural fiber mainly cultivated in West Bengal, Bihar, Assam, Odisha, and Uttar Pradesh. India is the largest producer of jute in the world, contributing significantly to the economy. Jute is used to make sacks, ropes, carpets, and packaging materials. It is eco-friendly and biodegradable, making it an excellent alternative to plastic. The jute industry provides employment to millions of farmers and workers. The crop is referred to as 'Golden Fibre' due to its economic importance and versatile uses.

question_hi: भारत में किस फसल को 'गोल्डन फाइबर' कहा जाता है? (RPF Constable 2024 (11/03/2025) Shift 1)
options_hi: रेशम

question: What is the coastal zone located in the western part of India, along the Arabian Sea and south of Goa, known as? (RPF Constable 2024 (11/03/2025) Shift 1)
options: Coromandel coast
Malabar coast
Konkan coast
Sunderbans
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Malabar coast

Explanation:
The western coastal region of India is divided into three parts: the Konkan coast (from Gujarat to Goa), the Malabar coast (south of Goa to Kanyakumari), and the Coromandel coast (eastern coast of Tamil Nadu). The area south of Goa along the Arabian Sea, as mentioned in the question, is the Malabar coast, which includes coastal parts of Kerala and Karnataka. This coast is famous for its coconut plantations, spices, and the slopes of the Western Ghats. The Sunderbans are the Ganges delta region in West Bengal. Thus, the coastal zone south of Goa is called the Malabar coast.

question: Which of the following has an interface of agriculture and industry and covers large tracts of land, using capital-intensive inputs with the help of migrant labourers? (RPF Constable 2024 (11/03/2025) Shift 2)
options: Plantation Farming
Primitive Subsistence Farming
Dryland Farming
Intensive Subsistence Farming
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Plantation Farming.

Explanation:
Plantation farming is an interface of agriculture and industry, covering large tracts of land using capital-intensive inputs and migrant labour. It grows cash crops like tea, coffee, rubber, and banana, which are processed by industries. This farming type developed during the colonial era and still thrives in developing countries. It involves extensive mechanisation, scientific techniques, and labour-intensive cultivation. In contrast, primitive subsistence farming is small-scale for self-sufficiency, dryland farming occurs in arid regions, and intensive subsistence farming is practised in densely populated areas with small landholdings. Plantation farming is categorised as a single-crop, large-scale commercial farming system that links agricultural production with industrial processing, often for export.

☛ Major crops in plantation farming → Tea, coffee, rubber, banana, sugarcane
☛ Labour source in plantation farming → Migrant labourers
☛ Industry linked to plantation farming → Processing industry
☛ Development period of plantation farming → Colonial era
☛ Type of plantation farming → Single-crop large-scale cash crop farming

question: The Standard Meridian of India (82°30'E), used to set the standard time for the entire country, passes through which of the following places? (RPF Constable 2024 (11/03/2025) Shift 2)
options: Kolkata
Jaipur
Mirzapur
Bhopal
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Mirzapur

Explanation:
The Standard Meridian of India is 82°30' East longitude, which passes through Mirzapur in Uttar Pradesh. It is adopted as the reference line for Indian Standard Time (IST), which is 5 hours 30 minutes ahead of Greenwich Mean Time (GMT). This meridian ensures uniform time across the country, although India's geographical extent spans nearly 30 longitudes.

question: In which state is Indira Sagar Hydroelectric Power Project located? (RPF Constable 2024 (11/03/2025) Shift 2)
options: Andhra Pradesh
Haryana
Madhya Pradesh
Bihar
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Madhya Pradesh

Explanation:
The Indira Sagar Hydroelectric Power Project is located in the Madhya Pradesh state, specifically in the Khandwa district on the Narmada River. It is a multipurpose project under the Narmada Valley Development, aimed at power generation and irrigation. The dam is 92 meters high, and the reservoir has a capacity of 12.22 billion cubic meters. The project has an installed capacity of 1000 MW, consisting of 8 units of 125 MW each. Construction was completed in 2004, and it is owned and operated by the Narmada Valley Development Authority and the Government of Madhya Pradesh. It is one of India's major hydropower projects.

question: National Waterway 2 (NW 2) is operational in which of the following Indian states? (RPF Constable 2024 (11/03/2025) Shift 2)
options: Arunachal Pradesh
Sikkim
Assam
Nagaland
solution:

Explanation:
National Waterway 2 (NW 2) is operational in the Indian state of Assam. It is located on the Brahmaputra River and extends from Sadiya to Dhubri for a distance of 891 km. This waterway serves as a vital transportation artery for the northeastern region, connecting remote areas that lack good road and rail networks. NW 2 is mainly used for transporting tea, coal, cement, and agricultural produce. It is administered by the Inland Waterways Authority of India (IWAI). The central government has developed this waterway to boost trade and economic development in the northeast region.

question: Which coastal plain of India is predominantly rocky? (RPF Constable 2024 (11/03/2025) Shift 2)
options: Western Coastal Plain
Northern Coastal Plain
Coromandel Plain
Eastern Coastal Plain
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Western Coastal Plain

Explanation:
The Western Coastal Plain of India is predominantly rocky. Stretching from Gujarat to Kerala, it has a rugged and uneven coastline due to the proximity of the Western Ghats. The plain is narrow and rocky, especially in the northern part known as the Konkan coast. In contrast, the Eastern Coastal Plain is wider and covered with alluvial soil brought by rivers. The Western Coastal Plain is divided into three sections: the Konkan coast (rocky), the Kannad plain, and the Malabar coast. The Malabar coast is relatively wider and has backwaters. Major natural harbors like Mumbai, Marmagao, and Kochi are located along this coast. The Coromandel Plain is part of the Eastern Coastal Plain and is not rocky. Understanding the distinct characteristics of India's coastal plains is important for geography exams.

question: In India, the Sundari tree is a prominent species found in which type of forests? (RPF Constable 2024 (11/03/2025) Shift 2)

Explanation:

question: The sun and other stars are mostly composed of which of the following states of matter? (RPF Constable 2024 (11/03/2025) Shift 3)
options: Plasma
Solid
Liquid
Gas
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Plasma

Explanation:
The sun and other stars are mostly composed of plasma, the fourth state of matter. Plasma is formed when gas particles become ionized due to extremely high temperatures, causing electrons to break free from atoms. In stars, the core temperature reaches millions of degrees (e.g., the Sun's core is about 15 million degrees Celsius), leading to ionization and plasma formation. Plasma conducts electricity and is influenced by magnetic fields. Over 99% of the visible universe is in plasma state. Examples of plasma on Earth include lightning, neon lights, and fluorescent bulbs. Nuclear fusion reactions that power stars occur only in plasma state. Unlike solids, liquids, or gases, plasma has unique properties due to free electrons and ions. Stars are thus vast balls of plasma undergoing fusion.

question: When was the first passenger train service in India started? (RPF Constable 2024 (11/03/2025) Shift 3)

question: The Luni River, flowing through the Thar Desert, eventually flows into: (RPF Constable 2024 (11/03/2025) Shift 3)

Palk Bay
Arabian Sea
Rann of Kutch
solution:

The river is seasonal and has no permanent flow to the sea.

question: In rural development, technology that can be added in development without displacing labour and at less expenditure is called _______. (RPF Constable 2024 (11/03/2025) Shift 3)
options: labour intensive technology
capital intensive technology
labour displacement technology
capital displacement technology
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is labour intensive technology

Explanation:
In rural development, labour intensive technology refers to a technique that can be added to development without displacing labour and at low cost. This technology uses more workers, thereby increasing employment opportunities and requiring less capital investment. It is considered suitable for rural areas in developing countries as it effectively utilizes local resources and skills. In contrast, capital intensive technology requires more machinery and capital investment, which may lead to labour displacement. Labour displacement technology makes workers unemployed, while capital displacement technology saves capital but is less common in rural development.

☛ What is reduced in labour intensive technology? → Capital expenditure

question: Which physiographic division of India includes the Great Indian Plains? (RPF Constable 2024 (11/03/2025) Shift 3)
options: The Coastal Plains
The Northern Plains
The Peninsular Plateau
The Northern Mountains
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is The Northern Plains

Explanation:
India's physiographic division consists of six major parts. Among them, the Northern Plains is the vast region located south of the Himalayas, formed by the Indus, Ganga, and Brahmaputra rivers. It is also known as the Himalayan Piedmont region and the Ganga Plain. This plain is fertile and considered the backbone of Indian agriculture. The Coastal Plains are located along the seashore, the Peninsular Plateau is the highland of southern India, and the Northern Mountains refer to the Himalayan range. Hence, the Great Indian Plains are included in the Northern Plains.

question: In which type of forest is scrub vegetation typically found in India? (RPF Constable 2024 (11/03/2025) Shift 3)

Montane forests
Littoral and Swamp forests
Tropical Evergreen forests
solution:

Explanation:

The trees are sparse and widely scattered, with thorny shrubs and bushes like Acacia, Cactus, and Euphorbia being dominant. These forests are mainly located in parts of Rajasthan, Gujarat, Punjab, Haryana, Madhya Pradesh, and some dry areas of the Deccan Plateau. The leaves are small and waxy to conserve water, adapting to the arid climate.

question:
Which of the following are the main reasons for the excessive cold in north India during the winter season?
(1) Presence of moderating influence of sea
(2) Snowfall in the Himalayan ranges
(3) Coming of cold winds from the Caspian Sea and Turkmenistan (RPF Constable 2024 (11/03/2025) Shift 3)
options: Only 2 and 3
Only 1 and 3
Only 1 and 2
1, 2 and 3
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Only 2 and 3

Explanation:
The main reasons for excessive cold in north India during winter are snowfall in the Himalayan ranges, which drives cold winds southward, and the inflow of cold winds from the Caspian Sea and Turkmenistan. The moderating influence of the sea (maritime effect) is absent in north India due to its inland location, so option 1 is incorrect. Therefore, reasons 2 and 3 are correct.

question: In the Thar Desert, inselbergs are: (RPF Constable 2024 (12/03/2025) Shift 1)
options: sand dunes shaped by monsoon winds
flat desert plains formed by wind erosion
riverbeds that are periodically dry
isolated rock hills rising sharply from the surrounding plain
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is isolated rock hills rising sharply from the surrounding plain

Explanation:
Inselbergs are isolated rock hills that rise abruptly from a flat plain. They are formed primarily by weathering and erosion, where softer surrounding rocks are worn away, leaving behind a resistant rock mass. In the Thar Desert, these landforms are remnants of ancient plateaus. Sand dunes, flat desert plains, and dry riverbeds do not qualify as inselbergs. Inselbergs are characteristic of arid and semi-arid regions.

question: Which of the following rivers is known for creating a rift valley in the Deccan Plateau and flows from Central India to the Arabian Sea? (RPF Constable 2024 (12/03/2025) Shift 1)
options: Mahi
Narmada
Godavari
Krishna
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Narmada

Explanation:
The Narmada River flows through a rift valley on the Deccan Plateau. It originates from the Amarkantak plateau in Madhya Pradesh and flows westward into the Arabian Sea. It is the second longest peninsular river after the Godavari. The Narmada and the Tapti are the only major rivers in peninsular India that flow westward. A rift valley is formed by a crack in the Earth's crust, with steep cliffs on both sides. The total length of the Narmada is about 1312 kilometers. It forms the traditional boundary between North and South India. Its major tributaries include Banas, Tawa, and Barna. The river is known for the Dhuandhar Falls and supports several hydroelectric projects.

question: Which initiative in the 1960s marked the beginning of technological advancement in agriculture in India? (RPF Constable 2024 (12/03/2025) Shift 1)
options: Land Reforms
Green Revolution
Industrial Licensing
New Industrial Policy
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Green Revolution

Explanation:
The Green Revolution in the 1960s marked the beginning of technological advancement in agriculture in India. It was led by scientists like M. S. Swaminathan and Norman Borlaug. The initiative involved the use of high-yielding variety seeds, especially for wheat and rice, along with chemical fertilizers and pesticides. Irrigation facilities were also expanded, leading to an unprecedented increase in agricultural productivity. The Green Revolution made India self-sufficient in food grains and helped the country overcome famine-like situations. It was a major shift in agricultural policy and technology, paving the way for other agricultural revolutions like the White and Blue Revolutions.

1960 के दशक में हरित क्रांति ने भारत में कृषि में तकनीकी प्रगति की शुरुआत की। इसका नेतृत्व एम. एस. स्वामीनाथन और नॉर्मन बोरलॉग जैसे वैज्ञानिकों ने किया। इसमें उच्च उपज देने वाली बीज किस्मों, विशेषकर गेहूं और चावल, के साथ-साथ रासायनिक उर्वरकों और कीटनाशकों का उपयोग किया गया। सिंचाई सुविधाओं का विस्तार भी किया गया, जिससे कृषि उत्पादकता में अभूतपूर्व वृद्धि हुई। हरित क्रांति ने भारत को खाद्यान्न में आत्मनिर्भर बनाया और देश को अकाल की स्थिति से उबारा। यह कृषि नीति और प्रौद्योगिकी में एक बड़ा बदलाव था, जिसने बाद में श्वेत और नीली क्रांति जैसे अन्य कृषि सुधारों का मार्ग प्रशस्त किया।
